text: When an order names a machine count but the real target is a rate (e.g. red science "at least 3" but checked at 30/min), size the build from the rate (packs/min ÷ per-machine rate: asm1 red science = 6/min each, so 5 for 30/min) and build that many in the first plan. Also check how far the feed belts actually run before laying a repeated row, and extend them in the same plan if the row reaches pas

When an order says "into a chest" at a rate, route every production unit's output into ONE shared chest (not one chest per unit), since the check counts packs in a single chest. End the first plan with a wait long enough to fill it to about 2 minutes of output, with an expect on that chest's count.

To swap a single entity for a better tier (e.g. one inserter to a fast inserter), don't use upgrade with radius 0/only; just mine_at the old one and place the new one with the same pickup/drop. Better still, pick the right tier in the first build (fast inserter wherever one inserter must carry a whole column's output, ~2.5 items/s).

For long pole runs (100+ tiles) with connect medium-electric-pole, legs can end just over wire reach from the next pole; after the connect, check that the far end is on the source grid and place a bridging pole wherever a hop exceeds 9 tiles (medium) / 7.5 (small). For long belts, add a wait of length/1.875 s (yellow) before expecting items at the far end.

When a player changes an order mid-job (e.g. which side of a belt to build on), don't resubmit the same cancelled layout: move the build to a fresh spot that clearly matches the new instruction and the order's hinted location, staying away from the leftover ghosts. Always add an explicit power step from the existing grid so the new spot gets power.

When fixing a brownout, size the new generation from the full peak demand of every consumer on the grid (machines at full power, inserters, and any electric-energy-interface or other unknown load), not from the current reading, which is capped by today's supply. Build capacity with clear headroom, e.g. a whole extra boiler with 2 engines, in the first plan.

Mining drills have no recipe, so never use a "working" check with recipe=<ore> for drills; verify a mine with belt_carries at the delivery end and has_item on the destination chest (plus powered near the drills).

When a plan gathers wood (or any resource) by clearing trees, a cleared tree yields only ~4 wood and a small patch may hold just 20-30 trees, so size the clear area from the total needed (count ÷ 4 trees) with a generous margin, e.g. radius 24, or follow it with a second clear. Put the gathering step before any step that uses the resource.

Before any step that spends a gathered resource, check that the gathering steps can supply the whole amount. Trees give about 4 wood each and a patch may hold only 20-30, so clear a radius of 24 or more, or several patches, until you have the total with margin.

When one assembler feeds several others (e.g. a gear assembler serving both the inserter and transport-belt assemblers), add up the plates/s its input inserter must carry; above ~0.8/s use fast inserters for that feed and its outputs from the start. For a rate target, size the build with ~50% headroom over the order (e.g. aim for 15/min when 10/min is asked), because direct-insertion chains run be

When adding a second boiler beside an existing one, place it so its water connection touches the first boiler's connection directly (no gap), or put a pipe in any gap between them. Expect a check that every new steam engine is working, not just the area powered, so a boiler or engine with no water gets caught.

When one buffer chest feeds a machine and also passes items on to a second chest for another machine, the pass-through inserter grabs everything and starves the first machine; limit the downstream chest to 1 slot (limit step) in the same plan, or give each consumer its own feed. Spread intermediates evenly between parallel machines from the start.

In direct-insertion chains (cable->circuit->inserter, gears feeding two assemblers), use fast inserters for every machine-to-machine and belt-to-intermediate link from the start, since basic inserters starve the chain well below the recipe rate. Aim the theoretical rate at ~1.5x the order and don't let a pass-through inserter feed one consumer's buffer from another's.

For a rate target with asm2, plan enough final assemblers for 1.5x the rate from the start (green science asm2 = 7.5/min each, so 3 for 10/min), and place each final assembler next to its suppliers so it's fed by direct insertion or a short belt you lay tile by tile in ghosts. Don't add one later with a connect through a crowded build, because the router picks its own path and can take the tiles y

Don't hand-place isolated poles at a remote outpost and expect them to wire to a long pole line: they may stay on their own dead grid. Power remote machines with one connect medium-electric-pole step from a grid pole a few hops back right to a tile beside the machines (then connect on from that last pole for the rest), and remove failed small-pole ghosts first since they can block those tiles.

When adding a boiler, feed it fuel the same way as the existing one (extend or split the existing coal belt to its inserter), not from a hand-stocked chest, because "storage" coal may be out of reach and infinity chests can be walled in. If a hand-stock really is needed, insert only what the character carries (check with me) instead of a large fixed count.

A power step's small-pole line can end one hop short of the grid (a gap just over 7.5 tiles) and leave the new poles on a dead grid. After any power step, check that the far pole is on the source grid; better, use medium poles or place a bridging pole yourself halfway between the last grid pole and the first new one.

When copying an earlier build, check that every link in the chain exists, especially the last one: the inserter (and its pole) from the end of the output belt into the chest. Build the missing links in the first plan, and check the result with has_item on each chest rather than trusting a count of planned buildings, since leftover ghosts from a failed copy make that count fail even when the build

When powering a new build from a grid pole more than ~9 tiles away, place your own medium-pole chain in the ghosts step with every hop under 8 tiles, starting right next to the grid pole, instead of relying on a power step (it can leave a hop just over reach and a dead grid).

A new production line needs several minutes before its rate and chest checks can pass, so end the first plan with a wait long enough for the slowest chain to fill (about 4-5 min for asm1 green science fed by intermediates). Set the expects to the order's real targets (packs per minute, intermediates made, chest count) so the first plan doesn't report done or failed before the line has ramped up.

Don't clear entities the order names as fixed endpoints (e.g. the destination chest) just to make room for a saved design; if you do clear them, add an explicit step to place them back after the design. Then check that the destination exists with has_item.

If a chest or other building stays an unbuilt ghost after a build_ghosts or place step, retrying the same step won't help. First mine_at the ghost tile (plus clear trees=true there), then place the building directly, preferably an iron chest rather than a wooden one.

A medium pole powers only 3 tiles each side of its own tile (a small pole 2), so before submitting hand-placed ghosts, check that every inserter and machine falls inside some pole's area. Watch especially the inserters in the gap row between two machine rows, which a pole one row too far off misses. When an order says "power it from the grid there", the machines must end up on that exact grid (the one at the named spot), not on some nearer grid that happens to have a generator; run the pole line all the way to a pole of the named grid. If there aren't enough poles, take up redundant or duplicate pole lines already in place and reuse them, rather than bridging to the closest live grid.

When the area shows a machine, chest or pole already standing where you want one (e.g. left over from an earlier build), don't put a ghost of it on the same spot; reuse it and only ghost the missing inserters, because a duplicate ghost stays unbuilt and inserters placed next to it lock onto the ghost and wait forever. If inserters say "waiting_for_target_to_be_built" beside a real building, mine_a

Before bridging to a copy of a saved design, check which pole type the design itself uses (it may be medium poles at a different offset than the original's small poles): a small pole links to anything only within 7.5 tiles. Place bridge poles so every hop from the grid to the design's own poles is under 7 tiles, ideally with medium poles.

When a plan needs fuel (wood or coal) and none is stored or carried, first use find to locate the nearest real source (find tree / coal) and gather a generous amount there before any fuel step. Then refuel every burner across all the sites that shows low or no fuel, not just the one that looks broken, since others will run dry during the plan.

When a new production line is checked by rate and chest count, end the first plan with a wait of at least 4-5 minutes (not 3) and expect counts that only pass once the line is steady, so the order isn't judged before it ramps up. If a later check shows zeros but the area shows the chest filling and the machines working, don't rebuild: just wait and re-check.

Build a production order right beside the input belts the order points at (tap them where it says they are, between or alongside them), not far downstream at their ends, because the order's checks only count machines and chests near the pointed locations. If the checks read zero while a far-off build is clearly working, rebuild it compactly at the pointed spot.

A connect pole line only guarantees power to the tile it ends at, so in the same ghosts step place a pole whose 5x5 (small) area covers every new inserter, especially the belt-side input inserter on the far side of the machine from where the pole line ends. Check each inserter tile against pole areas before submitting.

A "working" check counts only crafting machines (assemblers, furnaces), never inserters, belts or drills, so don't use it to verify an inserter or a mine. Check those with belt_carries on the last belt tile and has_item on the destination chest instead.

When the actor's copy reports leftover unbuilt ghosts but the area shows the real buildings at those spots working and the chests filling, don't re-place or mine them; submit only a wait of several minutes with expects on working machines and chest counts. If you need a better look, query a small area centred on each build, because big-radius summaries cut off and make finished builds look missing

Before rebuilding something that a big-area summary shows as missing, query a small area centred on each site (the summary often drops machines at its edges), and if the real buildings are there and working, submit only a wait with expects instead of ghosting duplicates. A medium pole powers only tiles within 3 of its own tile, so poles spaced 8 apart along a machine row leave the inserters halfway between them unpowered. When hand-placing poles in ghosts, list every inserter tile and confirm each is within 3 tiles (medium) or 2 tiles (small) of some pole, adding small poles in the gaps between machines wherever one isn't.
